leftEvidence.role: Confession, suffering, and the coming Kingdom
leftEvidence.title: Luke places prayer, confession, suffering, and glory together

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: While Jesus prays, Peter calls him God’s Christ; Jesus predicts rejection, death, and resurrection.
points.right: About eight days after the sayings Jesus takes Peter, John, and James up the mountain to pray; his face changes and his clothing flashes white.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Daily cross-bearing, future glory, and a promise that some will see God’s Kingdom lead into the next scene.
points.right: Moses and Elijah speak of his departure to be completed at Jerusalem; sleepy disciples see glory, Peter proposes tents, a cloud brings fear, and the voice names the chosen Son.

payload.posture: Luke places prayer, confession, suffering, future glory, and Kingdom sight before the prayer and glory of the mountain.

rightEvidence.title: Luke places prayer and an exodus conversation on the mountain

payload.tension: The later scene develops the approach without reducing every prior saying to itself.
payload.title: Glory promised and glory seen
